title: Specified point-transport cone comparison and descent through roofs
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}=\lim_n(A_n)_s$, and $\Gamma=\Gamma(s,-)$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. For a flat-term K-flat complex $P$ of $R$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], put $P_n=P\otimes_R(A_n)_s$, $r_n(x)=x\otimes1$, and $t_n=1\otimes(A_{n+1}\to A_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $C_n=\operatorname{Res}_ng_n^*P_n$, with the coefficient-induced transition $v_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b); put $D_n=\Gamma P_n$, $B_n=\Gamma C_n$. All these towers are over the single integral coefficient ring after restriction of scalars. For a strict tower $X_\bullet$ with transitions $w_n$ set $s_X((x_n)_n)=(w_nx_{n+1})_n$ and $H(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_X)[-1]$, with $H(X)^i=\prod_nX_n^{i-1}\oplus\prod_nX_n^i$ and $d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_X)a,da)$ [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. Let $N$ be a complex of $R$-modules and $q:P\to N$ a quasi-isomorphism. Use $\sigma$ of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] and $\theta_n=\kappa_{P_n}g^{-1}(r_n)$ of comparison (b) [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Suppose $u:D_\bullet\to B_\bullet$ is a strict tower map satisfying $\Gamma(\theta_n)\sigma_P=u_n\Gamma(r_n)$ for every $n$. Put $a_P(z)=(0,(\Gamma(r_n)z)_n)$ and $\widetilde\theta_P(w)=(0,(\theta_nw)_n)$; let $c_C:\Gamma H(C_\bullet)\to H(B_\bullet)$ be the identity on the two sectionwise product components. Then the following is a chain-map equality, including the shifted-product component:
$$c_C\Gamma(\widetilde\theta_P)\sigma_P=H(u)a_P.$$
Under the defining identification of completed $Lg^*N$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] with $H(C_\bullet)$, let $b_q:\Gamma Lg^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}H(B_\bullet)$ be induced by $c_C$. The specified integral comparison $\kappa_N=[\widetilde\theta_P][g^{-1}q]^{-1}$ and $\iota_N=\Gamma(\kappa_N)\sigma_N$ satisfy
$$b_q\iota_N\Gamma(q)=[H(u)a_P],\qquad b_q\iota_N=[H(u)a_P][\Gamma(q)]^{-1}.$$
Here exact sections make $\Gamma(q)$ invertible, and $\sigma_N\Gamma(q)=\Gamma(g^{-1}q)\sigma_P$. These identities compare the actual integral map of part (b), including its zero shifted-product component. If the family $u(P)$ commutes with chain maps between flat-term K-flat representatives, these identities are independent of those representatives under the specified completed-pullback comparison maps and are natural for arbitrary derived morphisms: for any roof $P\xleftarrow{a}Q\xrightarrow{b}P'$ with $a$ a quasi-isomorphism in that resolving class they commute with $[b][a]^{-1}$. No derived-completeness hypothesis on $[N]$ and no invertibility of $[a_P][\Gamma(q)]^{-1}$ is required.
